q: Who founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
e: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a slave of Muhammad Ghori, founded the dynasty in 1206.

q: Who was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
e: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240.

q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between:
e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi and founded Mughal rule in India.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
e: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after his victory at Panipat in 1526.

q: Which Mughal emperor started 'Din-i-Ilahi'?
e: Akbar started Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 as a blend of ideas from many faiths.

q: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by:
e: Akbar built it to celebrate his victory in Gujarat.

q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by:
e: Brothers Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336 (Sangama dynasty).

q: Who was the founder of Sikhism?
e: Guru Nanak Dev (1469-1539) was the first Sikh Guru.

q: The Khalsa Panth was founded in 1699 by:
e: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib.

q: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces and:
e: Akbar's army, led by Bairam Khan, defeated Hemu in 1556.

q: 'Ain-i-Akbari' was written by:
e: Abul Fazl wrote Ain-i-Akbari as part of the Akbarnama.

q: The famous Peacock Throne was made for which Mughal emperor?
e: Shah Jahan had the jewelled Peacock Throne made; Nadir Shah carried it away in 1739.

q: The construction of Qutub Minar was completed by:
e: Aibak began the Qutub Minar and his successor Iltutmish completed it.

q: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at:
e: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad fort in 1674.

q: Which Sultan introduced token currency of copper and brass coins?
e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued token coins, but the plan failed due to forgery.

q: Which Sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri)?
e: In 1327, Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Daulatabad.

q: In which year was the Battle of Haldighati fought?
e: Maharana Pratap fought Akbar's army led by Man Singh at Haldighati in 1576.

q: The Battle of Chausa (1539) was fought between:
o: Humayun and Bahadur Shah of Gujarat
e: Sher Shah defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and again at Kannauj in 1540.

q: Who introduced the Mansabdari system in the Mughal administration?
e: Akbar ranked officials by mansab (rank) that fixed their pay and troops.

q: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur was built by:
e: Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwaram) temple around 1010 AD.

q: Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of:
e: Ibn Battuta served as Qazi of Delhi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote 'Rihla'.

q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and:
e: Ahmad Shah Abdali of Afghanistan defeated the Marathas in 1761.

q: Saint Kabir, a disciple of Ramananda, was by profession a:
e: Kabir was brought up in a family of weavers in Varanasi.

q: Khwaja Moinuddin of Ajmer belonged to which Sufi order?
e: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti brought the Chishti order to India.

q: Who was Akbar's finance minister known for land revenue reforms?
e: Todar Mal developed the Zabti (Dahsala) system of land revenue.

q: Nadir Shah invaded India in 1739 during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
e: Nadir Shah sacked Delhi in 1739 when Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' was emperor.

q: Krishnadeva Raya of Vijayanagara belonged to which dynasty?
e: Krishnadeva Raya (1509-1529) was the greatest ruler of the Tuluva dynasty.

q: The title 'Gangaikonda Chola' is associated with:
e: Rajendra I took this title after his army reached the Ganga and founded Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

q: Which Delhi Sultan is credited with organising the 'Iqta' system as an institution?
e: Iltutmish made the Iqta (land assignment in place of salary) a regular system.

q: Which Sultan introduced the Persian customs of 'Sijda' and 'Paibos' at court?
e: Balban stressed royal dignity and introduced Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet).
